headline.text: Revenue growth is decelerating: guided 14% to 16% vs 24% reported

guided.text: Our external channel has gone from sub 10% of our overall LEAP services portfolio to call it mid-teens right now, and we expect that to grow to, say, 30% by the time we get to 2030.

signals.speaker: Operator (Liz)
signals.sentence: If you experience issues with the webcast slides refreshing, or there appears to be delays in the slide advancement, please hit F5 on your keyboard to refresh.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: The second quarter marked another quarter of significant growth driven by robust commercial services.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Revenue increased 24%, with CES up 27% and DPT up 16%.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Operating profit grew 18%, with both segments up at least high teens.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: EPS increased 22%, and free cash flow grew 43%, with conversion over 140%.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: These results close out an exceptional first half, with orders up 49%, revenue up 27%, EPS growing 24%, and free cash flow increasing 31%, with 115% conversion.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: With the first half, commercial services revenue up 32% and total engine deliveries up 31%.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We remain focused on advancing what matters most to our customers, delivering on robust demand and our backlog of over $210 billion while investing in both current and next-gen technologies to improve time on wing and cost of ownership.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Given the strength of our first half results and momentum for the remainder of the year, this morning, we're raising our 2026 guidance across the board.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: This supported F110 deliveries growing over 50% year-over-year in the second quarter.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Just last week, we held three Kaizens with GKN, a top supplier of fan cases and other key components, to break constraints tied to rate performance.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We worked collaboratively together to create detailed visual work instructions, increase capacity, and implemented a 3D inspection technology, which led to a 90% improvement in inspection time.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Work is now underway to sustain these results and build further momentum.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Across our turbine airfoils team, for example, we recently ran several Kaizens to improve the demand signal process.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Standardizing and reducing demand signals strengthens supplier confidence, and then using AI to automate the process, we cut the number of demand signals in half and reduced processing time by nearly 90% across 190 parts.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: This supported commercial services revenue up 32% in the first half, including record internal shop visit output in the second quarter and first half total engine deliveries up 31%, including LEAP engines up 41%.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We're also expanding capacity to meet growing aftermarket demand for LEAP as the installed base is expected to more than double between now and 2030.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We expect a gradual return to modest departures growth in the second half, and combined with our commercial services backlog of roughly $170 billion, we remain well-positioned for services growth in 2026 and beyond.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Demand continues to be robust for LEAP, our fastest-growing platform, as demonstrated by Copa Airlines recently selecting up to 120 LEAP-1B engines to power their growing fleet of 737 MAX aircraft.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We've also expanded our relationship with BETA Technologies, who joined the EPFD project last year to advance the modification of the EPFD aircraft.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Within defense, we continue to support robust demand for our services and products, both domestically and with allied partners, while advancing next-gen technologies.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We announced an agreement with Turkish Aerospace Industries to provide F404 engines for its HÜRJET advanced jet trainer program, and our CT7 engines were selected to power the U.K.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We completed an assembly readiness review for the XA102 adaptive cycle engine, a critical milestone that moves the program from design into assembly and test.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We continue to strengthen our position in the fast-growing collaborative combat aircraft, or CCA market, with our suite of products.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Both the GEK1500 and the GE426 achieved significant milestones to move to preliminary design review, bringing them closer to eventual flight on small and medium-thrust CCAs respectively.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We look forward to sharing more exciting wins and updates at the Farnborough Airshow next week.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Stepping back, we're focused on translating our unmatched experience and investments into value for our customers while driving long-term growth.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: GE Aerospace delivered another strong quarter, marked by double-digit growth across all key metrics.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Orders were up 17%, with CES up 18% and DPT up 12%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Revenue increased 24%, marking our fifth consecutive quarter of at least 20% growth.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: CES was up 27% and DPT grew 16%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Operating profit was $2.7 billion, up 18%, driven by services volume and price.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: As expected, margins decreased 130 basis points to 21.7% from installed engine growth, investments, and inflation.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: EPS was $2.02, up 22%, from increased operating profit, a lower tax rate, and a reduced share count.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Free cash flow was $3 billion, up 43%, from higher earnings and nearly a $200 million reduction in working capital and AD&A, including year-over-year favorability from tariffs.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Our results build on the strong first quarter, with year-to-date revenue up 27%, operating profit up nearly $800 million, largely driven by strong growth in commercial services, and free cash flow up over $1 billion.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Increase in operating profit drove $0.31 or over 85% of the improvement in EPS.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: The remainder of the EPS growth was driven by lower tax rate and reduction in share count.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Tax rate decreased two points to 16.7%, primarily from tax planning and benefit from recent tax legislation.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Share count was down 24 million from 2%, or 2% from our previously announced capital allocation actions.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: In the second quarter, orders grew 18%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Equipment was up 7% as some orders shifted to second half, while nearly doubling year-to-date.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Revenue increased 27%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Services grew 26%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Internal shop visit revenue grew 25% from higher volume, including LEAP internal shop visits up over 50% and widebody mix.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Spare parts sales increased over 25% from improved material availability that helped us fulfill strong customer demand, growth in LEAP external channel, and price.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Even with strong revenue growth, given robust orders, spare parts delinquencies, which represents shipments that have been delayed due to material availability constraints, grew 20% sequentially in the second quarter.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Equipment revenue grew 30%, with engine deliveries up 26%, including LEAP up 24%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Profit was $2.7 billion, up 20% from higher services volume and price.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: As expected, margins were down 160 basis points to 27.3% from installed engine growth, including GE9X investments and inflation.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Year-to-date, CES has delivered a very strong first half, with orders growth of over 50%, revenue growth of 30%, including services up 32%, and operating profit of $5 billion, up approximately $900 million year-over-year.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: In DPT, orders increased 12%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Revenue grew 16%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Defense and systems revenue was up 12%, driven by growth in both services and equipment, with engine deliveries up 7%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Propulsion and adaptive technologies grew 23%, with growth led by Avio Aero.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Profit grew 18%, and margins were up 30 basis points to 13.8% from increased volume and price, partially offset by mix investments and inflation.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: In the first half, DPT delivered solid results with orders growth of 40%, revenue growth of 17%, and operating profit of around $900 million, up 17%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We're expecting overall revenue to grow high teens, up from prior outlook of low double digits.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We expect CES growth of around 20%, up from prior outlook of mid-teens.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We now expect commercial services to grow low 20s, up from mid-teens.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: This provides us with ample visibility into demand to fulfill our outlook for 2026.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We now expect commercial equipment to grow around 20%, up from mid to high teens, with LEAP deliveries up high teens from 15% previously.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We expect DPT growth of low double digits, up from mid to high single digits.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Operating profit is now projected to be in a range of $10.55 billion-$10.75 billion, with improvement in both segments.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: CES operating profit is now expected to be in a range of $10.25 billion-$10.35 billion, up $400 million versus the high end of the prior guide.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: This reflects the drop-through of around $1 billion of improvement in commercial services revenue, partially offset by higher equipment growth.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We expect DPT profit to be in the range of $1.6 billion-$1.7 billion, up $50 million at the midpoint versus the prior guide, reflecting drop-through from higher revenue.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: This reflects higher profit combined with a lower tax rate, which we now expect to be below 16.5% for the year.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We are also raising our free cash flow guidance to $8.9 billion-$9.2 billion, up $650 million from the high end of the prior guide, reflecting higher earnings and better working capital performance.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Overall, 2026 is shaping up to be another strong year with high teens revenue growth and around $1.5 billion of profit and free cash flow growth, building on the momentum the business has had in the last few years.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We're proud of the progress we've made in the first half.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: It reflects the strength of our leadership positions across commercial and defense, and the continued focus of the GE Aerospace team to deliver for our customers.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Our performance is underpinned by our sustained competitive advantages.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: With the industry's largest fleet, 80,000 engines and growing, and more than 2.3 billion flight hours, we operate across decades-long life cycles.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: That unmatched scale keeps us close to our customers, making us the partner of choice.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We offer the best-performing products under wing across narrow body, wide body, regional, and defense, supported by deep technology expertise and a growing services network.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: With roughly $3 billion in annual R&D spend and CapEx investments of over a billion dollars, our world-class engineering and manufacturing teams are advancing next-gen technologies to improve durability, efficiency, and turnaround times while building additional capabilities for our defense customers through developing innovative technologies and partnering with disruptors to move at pace.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Overall, we're confident in our path ahead as the GE Aerospace team is poised to deliver exceptional value to our customers and our shareholders.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: As we look at where we are, as we said in our prepared remarks, I think we feel very good about our position here, largely on the back of customer behavior, which hasn't changed.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Parked aircraft, particularly the CFM56, has actually declined since the beginning of March.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: As much as we're pleased with the delivery increases, our spare parts delinquencies are up, unfortunately.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: I think on the back of that, and I don't suspect we'll hear much different in Farnborough, we do expect a return to more modest departure growth in the second half.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We saw a relatively flattish performance, a little bit of the uncertainty that kept us holding the guide 90 days ago.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Sheila, to your second question on the first half to second half, as you said, that very strong first half for services, both on orders and revenue.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We raised our full-year guide to the low 20% growth, and now we're expecting services to be up $5 billion year-over-year.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: This is up about $1 billion from where we were just back in April, which is what led to us improving the CES profit outlook by, call it, say, $400 million from the high end of the prior guide.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Even with that, there is sequential growth from first half to second half of 2026.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: On a year-over-year basis, the second half services revenue in our current guide is up low double-digit from a very strong second half last year.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: As Larry Culp said, we feel very comfortable with where we are with the current guide, and as I said in my prepared remarks, 95% of our spare parts are in the backlog for third quarter.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: All in all, we feel very good, and it's great that we're driving double-digit growth for services in the second half, and that momentum should carry us into 2027, as Larry Culp said a minute ago.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We're really pleased with how we performed in the second quarter.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Cash flow of $3 billion, up 43% year-over-year.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: The best part for all of us was that we were able to reduce our working capital in the quarter, even with 24% earnings growth.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: A little bit of help from tariffs, which we got $100 million of refund from tariffs in the quarter, but in the grand scheme of things, that's not extremely material.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: I think we feel good about our working capital performance, and there's no huge one-time items in nature, so we do expect cash flow to grow here with earnings, but the conversion should normalize.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Conversion should normalize, but even with that, we expect significant cash growth as our earnings grow.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Thrilled to see not only nine consecutive quarters with double-digit increases from our critical suppliers, but maybe more importantly, the underlying work, the deep technical collaboration and joint problem-solving that we see underway.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Hopefully, we're a better partner, we're a better customer, and that is just unlocking, unleashing capacity.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: I won't recite some of the demand numbers that we've shared, as we think about the back half, as we think about 2027, frankly, beyond, it's much more a supply-side challenge than it is demand.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Not that we would ever take the demand environment for granted, we know, despite this morning's news, we need to have a bigger, better second half.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: I think if we just focus on services for a moment, we no longer term that in addition to that backlog that we've talked about, $170 billion commercially, the installed base should continue to grow gradually every year at a low to mid-single-digit rate.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We know with LEAP becoming a larger part of the installed base, eclipsing the CFM56, we know we'll get the GEnx doubling between now or really between 2024 and 2030, that that installed base with our growth platforms is definitely going to grow.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Work scope, we believe, is a structural tailwind, largely as a function of the natural aging of the installed base.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: I think we said earlier, this spring, this summer, no reason 2027 should diverge from that double-digit commercial services growth medium-term outlook, even as we go into next year, what will clearly be a higher trimming off point than we imagined.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We're mindful of that, but with our backlog, with that framework, that algorithm in place, and just the overall tone we're hearing from customers, I think we feel very good about where we are at this point.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Perhaps we know more definitively that that lesson from the pandemic that we've touched on a few times over the last several months, which was certainly in the air at Rio, at IATA, that we need to make sure we are prepared for the other side of the uncertainty, has really played out.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: There's just no way, I think, in the moment, given the uncertainty, just given the headlines, that we would have been well-served with investors to get out with an early bump in the guide.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We know how the market has responded to the uncertainty, to the dynamic conditions that are clearly out there.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: All the while, we continue to do what we do from an execution perspective, not taking anything for granted, but also knowing that with the backlog, with demand remaining robust, that we needed to continue to invest, we need to continue to procure, we need to continue with our FLIGHT DECK work.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: I think we'd play it the same way all over again and are thrilled to see the resiliency and demand and expect that that helps give us a little bit of a lens on how the second half is likely to evolve.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: I think on shop visits, as you said, we are expecting the shop visits to probably grow at kind of a 25% CAGR from now till 2030, and it's all a function of the installed base that's largely out there and will continue to grow over the next couple of years.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Most of the engines that we are shipping now are probably not going to come in for a shop visit between now and 2030.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: It's largely a function of the installed base that exists in the globe today.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: With that, the big change that we are going to see is that our external channel is going to continue to grow.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Our external channel has gone from sub 10% of our overall LEAP services portfolio to call it mid-teens right now, and we expect that to grow to, say, 30% by the time we get to 2030.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: That will continue to build, and all we are doing on our side is continuing to invest, to build more capacity, and then we are adding more channel partners.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: One, the fact is that we will be leveraging our fixed cost investments more as volume continues to grow.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We're investing in repairs to bring that shop visit cost down because, as you know, repairs help both with the turnaround time and the cost.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: David, I would just maybe step back on the durability kit, for a moment, whether it be at IATA a few weeks ago, whether it's a recent customer survey that we've done, I think we're encouraged with some of the feedback we're getting.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Internally, we've said one of our priorities for the year is to be more customer driven, to really see ourselves as our customers do.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: It really won't be something that will trigger an acceleration of work.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Well, again, in many respects, be it on the wide body side, be it on the narrow body side, it really is a function of the natural aging of the installed base.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: Even with some of the older platforms, you look at the GE90, for example, 70% of that installed base has yet to see shop visit two, which has a significant step up in work scope.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: As we work through the next several years, I think we'll see those engines come back, and again, that structural support, that tailwind will be helpful.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: The growth largely is coming from better volume, better price, and higher material availability.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: The material availability is what's driving the growth in CFM56 in a big way.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We'll see you there.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: The way we think about our own pricing is that we make significant investments, and we add a lot of capability to our customers, and we want to be rewarded for that.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: At the same time, we are facing inflationary headwinds as well.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Then obviously longer term, we continue to get incremental pricing as we kind of moving away from those initial launch phases of LEAP, NG, NX pricing, the dollar per shop visit on those platforms has grown over the years, that we've discussed previously.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Strong installed engine growth both last year, this year, I'd expect that to continue.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Margins are getting better this year, both in the first half and expecting full-year margin expansion on LEAP.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Overall, we expect, still below overall CES service margins, and that is putting a little bit of pressure on our margins.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: The third, and perhaps the biggest, is GE9X. Initial units, highest cost units, we started shipping those out last year, more this year.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: That volume will grow.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: That is because our services portfolio is the biggest part of the portfolio, it's the highest margin, and it drives the highest dollar growth.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: As those headwinds abate, the inherent mix advantage that we have in our business continues.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Overall, both for CES and for the total company, we would expect margin expansion in 2028 and beyond.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: I think what I was encouraged by in IATA, and also in some of the recent customer feedback that we've got, is I think people see us here in the short term doing all that we can to support them.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We've got LEAP AOGs, Aircraft On the Ground, down to near zero at the moment, despite the fact that the durability kit is not fully installed.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: That 34% for first half this year is actually an acceleration from what we saw in the first half of last year on a year-over-year basis, and even the second half of last year.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: We've seen continued sequential growth, continued acceleration of trends in service orders.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: I think the momentum is very strong.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Obviously, we spoke about the delinquency being up even with the 34% growth in spare parts orders for the first half, and delinquency is up 20%.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: Overall, I think we feel very comfortable with the outlook.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: On spares, Rob, overall, listen, we are seeing some normalization, but the number of spare engines that we are shipping, they continue to grow up.

signals.speaker: Rahul Ghai
signals.sentence: They continue to grow.

signals.speaker: Larry Culp
signals.sentence: We have more to do, but are confident in our path ahead in the long-term value creation for both our customers and our shareholders.
